Not scored; the work is internally coherent weight-training research, so this is a scope ruling, not a quality judgment.

paper.title: TTCS: Test-Time Curriculum Synthesis for Self-Evolving
paper.central_claim: TTCS co-evolves a question synthesizer and a reasoning solver, both initialized from the same pretrained model and trained online with GRPO at test time: the synthesizer generates question variants near the solver's capability frontier, and the solver trains on a mixture of test and synthetic questions with self-consistency rewards, yielding more reliable pseudo-labels and stabler test-time training than TTRL and R-Zero on competition math and transfer to general-domain reasoning.

evidence.quote: the solver updates itself using self-consistency rewards computed from multiple sampled responses on both original test and synthetic questions
evidence.support_explanation: Solver is updated by RL on majority-vote pseudo-label rewards; the update is to model parameters.

evidence.quote: enables dynamic parameter adaptation on unlabeled test instances by optimizing a self-supervised objective, which is typically constructed via majority voting
evidence.support_explanation: TTRL/TTCS family adapts parameters at test time.

evidence.quote: Both agents are optimized online via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
evidence.support_explanation: Both synthesizer and solver are trained by RL on weights; no non-weight artifact is retained.

evidence.quote: Unlike standard inference with fixed parameters, TTT enables the model to dynamically adapt its parameters only using test questions.
evidence.support_explanation: Confirms the persistent change is in parameters, and that the adaptation set is the test questions (transductive setting).

evidence.quote: TTCS elevates the average points from 17.30 to 41.49
evidence.support_explanation: Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B average; author-reported gain of the weight-trained model on the same test benchmarks used for adaptation.

evidence.quote: we additionally use GPT-4o-mini to assist in judging whether the predicted answer matches the ground truth.
the static 14B synthesizer yields only a limited improvement of +2.66 points
evidence.support_explanation: Co-evolving synthesizer vs frozen stronger synthesizer comparison on the 1.5B model.

evidence.support_explanation: Cross-benchmark transfer after test-time training on a different test set.

signatures.object: Synthesizer and solver LLM policies (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B/7B and a third backbone) initialized from one pretrained model
signatures.information: Unlabeled test questions; solver's own sampled answers (K samples) for self-consistency; no ground-truth labels at training time
signatures.operation: Synthesizer generates variants of each test question and is rewarded for solver self-consistency near 0.5 (variance-driven capability reward) minus similarity penalties; solver trains on test plus synthetic questions with majority-vote pseudo-label rewards and a consistency-based online filter; both by GRPO
signatures.output: Updated synthesizer and solver weights per iteration
signatures.conditions: Verifiable-answer math; small test sets; strong enough base for majority votes on variants
signatures.selection_rule_data: Capability-band reward and online data filter on the solver's rollout agreement
signatures.later_use: Next iteration's policies; evaluation of the adapted solver
signatures.failure_boundary: Adaptation on the same test questions that are evaluated (transductive); R-Zero instability; collapse risk handled by similarity penalties and test-question resampling

gap.author_gap: TTRL on difficult test questions yields wrong majority-vote consensus (unreliable pseudo-labels) and lacks learnable intermediate samples.
gap.checked_gap: Not evaluated: harness-scope gap check is not applicable because the contribution is a weight-training procedure.

matches.reason: The manufactured object is a training distribution of self-generated variants filtered by solver consistency, with learner-to-generator feedback.
